Tosafot on Bava Batra 46a:1:1.english: Rather, is it not [a case] where there are no witnesses? - Rivam asked: How can [the Gemara] rule [that the craftsman is believed] in a case where there are no witnesses? If so, why, [when the claim is made] within the time [of the hire], does [the worker] swear and collect? Don't we say at the beginning of [the chapter] Kol HaNishba'in (Shevuot 45b, and there) that if he hired him without witnesses, since [the employer] could say, "I never hired you," he can [instead] say to him, "I hired you and I gave you your wages"? And Ri answered that this is not difficult at all: First, it is a matter of dispute there; and furthermore, here that migo does not exist, since [the employer] admits to part [of the claim]; and if he were to say, "I never hired you," he would be denying the entire claim, and there is a presumption that a person does not brazenly defy his creditor to his face:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 46a:4:1.hebrew: אי דאיכא עדים אחר אמאי יש לו חזקה - ונראה דבראה מיירי, דאי בלא ראה אומן נמי יש לו חזקה מיגו דאי בעי אמר: החזרתיו לך, דאין צריך להחזיר לו בעדים. אלא ודאי בראה מיירי. א"כ אחר אמאי יש לו חזקה? כיון דאיכא עדים דבתורת פקדון בא לידו, ולא מצי למיטען נמי: החזרתי לך, שהרי ראה. ופר"ת נראה לר"י מאד רחוק, על כן לא כתבתיו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 46a:4:1.english: "If there are witnesses, why does another [person] have a *chazakah*?" - And it appears that [the Gemara] is speaking of a case where [the owner] saw [the craftsman take the item], for if he did not see, the craftsman too would have a *chazakah*, by virtue of a *migo*: for if he wished, he could say, "I returned it to you," since he is not required to return it to him in front of witnesses. Rather, it must certainly be speaking of a case where [the owner] saw. If so, why does another [person] have a *chazakah*? Since there are witnesses that it came into his hand as a deposit, and he also cannot claim, "I returned it to you," since [the owner] saw [that he did not]. And the explanation of Rabbeinu Tam seems to Rabbi Yitzchak [the Ri] very far-fetched, therefore I did not write it.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 46a:6:1.hebrew: וכי אין אדם עשוי לומר לאומן מכור לי טליתי - וטעה אומן ומכר את של זה, שהיה סבור למכור את של חבירו, ונתן לו את של חבירו תחתיו. אבל אם לא היה עשוי לומר לאומן למכור, לא היה מותר מחמת שטעה אומן ונתן את שלו לחבירו, דהוי כנתחלפו לו בבית האבל או בבית המשתה, וסופו שיחזיר חבירו את שלו לאומן, ויחזור ויתבע ממנו טליתו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 46a:6:1.english: "And is a person not likely to say to a craftsman, 'Sell my cloak for me'?" - [The case is that] the craftsman erred and sold this one's [cloak], since he thought he was selling that of the other person, and he gave this one the other person's [money or cloak] in its place. But if a person were not likely to tell a craftsman to sell, [keeping what he received] would not be permitted, because the craftsman erred and gave this one's own [cloak] to the other person. For it would be like [items] that were switched for him at a house of mourning or at a banquet, and in the end the other person would return what is his to the craftsman, and [the first person] would come back and claim his cloak from him [the craftsman].

Tosafot on Bava Batra 46a:8:1.hebrew: הא אית לי סהדי דחזיוה גבך - פי': טלית שהיו בו סימנים כעין שלי, ולא שהיה להם טביעות עין שהיו מכירים שהיא שלו:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 46a:8:1.english: "But I have witnesses who saw it with you" - Explanation: [they saw] a cloak that had signs resembling those of mine, and not that they had visual recognition (tevi'at ayin), such that they recognized that it was his.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 46a:9:1.hebrew: שפיר קאמר ליה - דלא משוי ראה. מ"ט? דראה תניא. תימה לרשב"א, דמאי בעי למימר? אי בעי למימר "שפיר קאמר" דלא משוי ליה ראה, דלא בעי לאפוקי דנחזייה — דמה צריך למימר עלה "ראה תניא"? פשיטא דאי מפיק ליה ויכירוה שהיא שלו, דחייב להחזיר, שהרי כפר ואמר "לא היו דברים מעולם"! ונראה לו לפרש הכי: שפיר קאמר, כלומר שטוען טענה זו, "לא היו דברים מעולם", דעל ידי כך לא משוי ליה ראה, הואיל ולעדים לא היה בה טביעות עין, ויכול לומר: אחר היה. אבל אי הוה טעין "לקוח הוא בידי", לא היה נאמן, דאין לו עוד מיגו — דאי בעי, אמר "החזרתיו לך" או "לא היו דברים מעולם", דירא לומר כן, הואיל ויש עדים שראו טלית כאותו שהוא שלו בידו. והשתא אתי שפיר דקאמר "מ"ט? ראה תניא", כלומר: אע"פ שאינה ראיה גמורה של טביעות עין, אלא שהיו בה סימנין כמו שלו, "ראה" דקתני בברייתא משמע ליה בכל ענין ראיה (גמורה) — אינו נאמן לומר "לקוח הוא בידי":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 46a:9:1.english: "He spoke well to him" - [meaning] that he does not render it "he saw." What is the reason [that it is different if he saw]? Because "he saw" was taught [in the baraita]. Rashba found this puzzling: What does [Rava] mean to say? If he means to say "he spoke well" because he did not render it a case of "he saw," in that he does not want to have it taken out so that we may examine it — what need is there to say about this, "'he saw' was taught"? It is obvious that if he takes it out and they recognize that it is his, he is obligated to return it, since he denied and said, "There were never any dealings"! And it seems to him [Rashba] that one should explain it thus: He spoke well — that is, that he makes this claim, "There were never any dealings," because through this he does not render it a case of "he saw," since the witnesses had no identification by eye of it, and he can say, "It was a different one." But if he were to claim, "It was purchased by me [and is] in my possession," he would not be believed, since he would no longer have another *migo* — for if he wished, he could say, "I returned it to you," or "There were never any dealings," [but] he is afraid to say so, since there are witnesses who saw a garment like the one that is his in his hand. And now it fits well that [the Gemara] says, "What is the reason? 'He saw' was taught," meaning: even though it is not a complete proof of identification by eye, but only that it had signs like his, the word "saw" that is taught in the baraita implies to him [that] in any case of seeing (complete) he is not believed to say, "It was purchased by me."
